mainTopic: Immersing כלים בתוך כלים: the reasons of רבא and רבי אילא, why the rule applies only to קודש, and the concern for איבה with an עם הארץ
overview: The משנה taught that for קודש one may not immerse vessels inside other vessels. רבי אילא said the worry is חציצה, something blocking the water. רבא said it is a גזירה in case someone immerses tiny items in a narrow-mouthed vessel, whose water is not connected to the מקוה. The practical difference between them is a basket full of vessels: רבי אילא forbids it, and רבא permits it. The גמרא adds that an impure outer vessel carries its טבילה to the vessels inside it, and it shows that the same argument appears among תנאים. Next it asks why the rule covers only קודש and not תרומה. After several rounds of questions and answers about חברים, the עם הארץ, and איבה (resentment), it traces the concern for איבה to רבי יוסי. רב פפא says that accepting testimony from an עם הארץ today follows רבי יוסי. Finally, the גמרא raises a worry about borrowing an עם הארץ's vessels and quotes a משנה where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about his earthenware vessel. That argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The size of an opening that connects water
steps.stepSummary: The end of the source רבא relies on: an opening connects two bodies of water only if it is as wide as a wineskin tube, enough for two fingers to turn inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and its inner space must be wide enough for two fingers to turn around in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a משנה about מקוה water that רבא brought to back up his reason. It gives the exact size of the opening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water passing through a hole counts as connected to the מקוה only if the hole is as wide as שפופרת הנוד, about two fingers that can turn inside. So water inside a narrow-mouthed vessel is not connected to the מקוה, and small items in it are not really immersed. That is why רבא says the חכמים made a גזירה against immersing vessels inside vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: Its hollow, the open space inside the tube
Fingers
Turning around in their place, twisting inside the opening
The tube or spout of a wineskin, the standard size for connecting water

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a quote. The words before it, about the wineskin tube and its thickness, came right before this section. Here we only get the end of the measurement.

phrases.english: and like its inner space,
phrases.notes: This means the hollow of the wineskin tube mentioned just before this line.

phrases.english: enough for two fingers to turn around in their place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the source רבא quoted, from just before this section, to support his reason of a גזירה.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's explanation that the ban on כלים בתוך כלים is a גזירה about narrow-mouthed vessels
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מקואות that water connects only through an opening the size of שפופרת הנוד, wide enough for two fingers to turn inside

steps.title: רבא follows the count of eleven stringencies
steps.stepSummary: רבא's view fits רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה, who counts eleven stringencies in the משנה: the first six apply to קודש and to חולין prepared in קודש purity, and the last ones apply only to real קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא holds like what רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: eleven stringencies are taught here. The first six apply both to קודש and to חולין prepared with the purity of קודש. The last ones apply to קודש but not to חולין prepared with the purity of קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבא's explanation matches a different count of the משנה's stringencies, eleven instead of רבי אילא's ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because רבא gives a different reason for the vessels-inside-vessels rule, he must divide the משנה's list differently from רבי אילא. He follows רב נחמן's count: eleven stringencies, six of which also apply to חולין handled with קודש-level purity. The rest apply only to real קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like this, his view fits this other opinion
Stringencies, extra levels of strictness for קודש
Ordinary food that someone chose to handle with the purity standards of קודש
They taught here, in this משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a disagreement about the reason behind one rule can change how the whole list of stringencies in the משנה is counted and applied.

phrases.english: He holds like this
phrases.notes: "He" is רבא, whose reason we just heard.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: that Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
Eleven stringencies were taught here:
phrases.notes: This is instead of רבי אילא's count of ten, from the previous amud.

phrases.english: The first six apply both to sacred food,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקּוֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: and to ordinary food prepared with the purity of sacred food.
The last ones apply to sacred food,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא לְחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקּוֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: but not to ordinary food prepared with the purity of sacred food.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּהָא דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving רבא's reason and source, the גמרא shows which count of the משנה's list his view fits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה lists eleven stringencies. The first six apply also to חולין prepared in קודש purity, and the rest apply only to real קודש.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between רבא and רבי אילא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבא's reason (a גזירה about narrow-mouthed vessels) and רבי אילא's reason (חציצה).
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference is there between רבא and רבי אילא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking for a real case where the two reasons would give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבא and רבי אילא agree that vessels may not be immersed inside vessels for קודש. They only disagree about why. The גמרא wants a case where the different reasons lead to different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there between, what is the practical difference
The אמורא who explained the rule as a concern of חציצה

phrases.english: What difference is there between
the view of Rava and the view of Rabbi Ila?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין דְּרָבָא לִדְרַבִּי אִילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having laid out רבא's reason next to רבי אילא's, the גמרא asks how they differ in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the חציצה reason and the narrow-mouth גזירה reason lead to different rulings

steps.title: A basket full of vessels: רבי אילא forbids
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a basket or wicker bin filled with vessels and immersed. According to רבי אילא, who worries about חציצה, the problem is still there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a basket or wicker bin that someone filled with vessels and immersed. According to the one who says the reason is חציצה, the problem exists here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by naming a case, a basket full of vessels, and first explains רבי אילא's side: it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry is חציצה, the weight of the vessels inside can press against the basket and block the water from reaching every spot. A wide basket does not help with that. So according to רבי אילא, immersing this way is still forbidden for קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Basket
A wicker bin or large woven container
Something blocking the water from touching the item being immersed
According to the one who says

phrases.english: The difference between them is
a basket or a wicker bin
that someone filled with vessels and immersed them.
According to the one who says it is because of blocking, the problem exists.
phrases.notes: That is רבי אילא. The vessels inside can weigh on the basket and keep the water out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ סַל וְגַרְגוּתְנִי שֶׁמִּילְּאָן כֵּלִים וְהִטְבִּילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving the case and applying רבי אילא's reason to it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A basket or wicker bin full of vessels. Under רבי אילא's חציצה reason it is still forbidden.

steps.title: A basket full of vessels: רבא permits
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, the גזירה is only about narrow-mouthed vessels. Baskets and bins are never that narrow, so the גזירה does not apply to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says it is a גזירה, in case someone immerses needles and hooks in a vessel whose mouth is narrower than a wineskin tube: there is no such thing as a basket or bin whose mouth is narrower than a wineskin tube, so there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer with רבא's side: a basket full of vessels is allowed, because his גזירה never covers wide containers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's worry is only that small items might sit in a vessel whose opening is too narrow to connect to the מקוה. A basket or bin always has a wide opening, so the water inside is connected. That is the practical difference: רבי אילא forbids this case and רבא permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rule the חכמים made to prevent a mistake
Needles
Hooks or small pointed tools
There is not, the problem does not exist

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבא and רבי אילא forbid כלים בתוך כלים for קודש, but for different reasons. רבי אילא worries about חציצה, so even a basket full of vessels is a problem. רבא worries only about narrow-mouthed vessels, so a basket or bin is fine.

phrases.english: According to the one who says it is because of a protective decree
in case someone immerses needles and hooks
in a vessel whose mouth is not as wide as a wineskin tube,
a basket or a wicker bin
whose mouth is not as wide as a wineskin tube does not exist.
phrases.notes: Baskets always have a wide opening, so רבא's decree never reaches them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַטְבִּיל מְחָטִין וְצִינּוֹרִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by applying רבא's reason to the same case, which shows the contrast.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under רבא's גזירה reason, a basket or bin full of vessels is permitted, since no basket has a mouth narrower than a wineskin tube.

steps.title: רבא stays consistent: vessels immersed inside a basket are pure
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that small vessels placed in a basket or wicker bin and immersed are pure. This fits his earlier reason, which is a גזירה only about narrow-mouthed vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא follows his own reasoning, because רבא said: a basket or wicker bin that someone filled with vessels and immersed, the vessels are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another statement of רבא to show that he really holds what we just said in his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 we said that, according to רבא, baskets and bins are not covered by the גזירה because they are never narrow-mouthed. Here רבא says this himself: vessels immersed inside a basket are fully pure. So his ruling matches his reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (he stays consistent)
Basket
Wicker bin, a woven container
He immersed them

phrases.english: And Rava follows his own reasoning,
as Rava said:
A basket or a wicker bin
that one filled with vessels and immersed them
they are pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the view given to רבא in Step 5 using his own ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessels immersed inside a basket or wicker bin are pure.

steps.title: A basket or bin cannot join two halves of a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: If a basket or bin splits a מקוה into two parts, a person who immerses there has not done a valid טבילה. Water seeping through does not join the two parts, just as water seeping through the ground does not join separate pools.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if a מקוה was divided by a basket or wicker bin, someone who immerses there has not done a valid טבילה. The whole ground lets water seep through it, and still we require forty סאה in one place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second ruling about baskets and bins. This time the basket divides a מקוה, and he explains why the טבילה does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A basket is full of holes, but water seeping through holes is not a real connection. רבא proves this from the ground: water seeps through all soil, yet separate pools are never counted together. A מקוה needs forty סאה gathered in one place.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual bath
He divided it
His immersion does not count
It is full of holes, porous (water seeps through)
Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict Step 6. In Step 6 the basket sits inside one full מקוה, so the water is fine. Here the basket splits the מקוה, and neither part has forty סאה alone.

phrases.english: And a mikveh that one divided with a basket or wicker bin
one who immerses there,
his immersion does not count.
For the whole earth is porous,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָעֵינַן דְּאִיכָּא אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: and yet we require that there be forty se'ah in one place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of רבא about baskets and bins, said together with the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A basket or bin dividing a מקוה does not join the parts; the טבילה is invalid unless forty סאה are in one place.

steps.title: The narrow-mouth rule applies only to a pure outer vessel
steps.stepSummary: The rule against immersing small vessels inside a narrow-mouthed vessel applies only when the outer vessel is pure. If the outer vessel is impure, its own טבילה also works for the vessels inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to a pure vessel. But with an impure vessel, since the טבילה works for the whole outer vessel, it also works for the vessels inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a limit on the narrow-mouthed vessel rule. It applies only when the outer vessel is already pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An impure outer vessel needs טבילה itself, and water must reach every part of it, including the inside. Since that water counts as connected to the מקוה for the outer vessel, it also counts as connected for the small vessels inside. A pure outer vessel does not need טבילה, so this reasoning does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only (introduces a limit on the rule)
Since (since it works for one thing, it also works for another)
It works, it takes effect
Vessel

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the outer vessel's own status decides the case. An impure outer vessel 'carries' the טבילה to whatever is inside it.

phrases.english: And this applies to a pure vessel,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the rule from before: small vessels like needles cannot be immersed inside a narrow-mouthed vessel.

phrases.english: but with an impure vessel,
since the immersion works
for the whole body of the vessel,
it also works
for the vessels that are inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּכְלִי טָהוֹר, אֲבָל בִּכְלִי טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the narrow-mouthed vessel rule discussed earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The narrow-mouth problem applies only when the outer vessel is pure; an impure outer vessel's טבילה works for the vessels inside it.

steps.title: A משנה supports the pure/impure distinction
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in מקואות says that vessels filled with vessels and immersed are pure. It then says that, if he did not immerse, the waters are joined only through an opening as wide as a wineskin tube.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: vessels that one filled with vessels and immersed are pure. And if he did not immerse, waters are not joined until they are joined like the tube of a wineskin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as proof for the distinction it just made between an impure outer vessel and a pure one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה says the vessels are pure with no limit on the width of the opening. That fits the case where the outer vessel itself needs טבילה. The second part brings back the wineskin-tube width, but its wording, 'and if he did not immerse', is unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (in a משנה)
Waters that are joined together
The tube of a wineskin, the minimum width for joining waters

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishnah:
Vessels that one filled with vessels and immersed them
these are pure.
And if he did not immerse,
waters that are joined
are not joined until they are joined like the tube of a wineskin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support the limit given in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction between an impure outer vessel (no width needed) and a pure one (wineskin-tube width needed).

steps.title: What does 'and if he did not immerse' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'and if he did not immerse'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the משנה saying with 'and if he did not immerse'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the unclear wording in the משנה. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, 'if he did not immerse' makes no sense, because the whole case is about immersing. The גמרא needs to know which case the משנה means before the proof can work.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying?

phrases.english: What is it saying
with 'and if he did not immerse'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unclear second part of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'and if he did not immerse' in the משנה.

steps.title: It means: if the outer vessel did not need immersion
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means: if the outer vessel did not need טבילה because it was already pure, then, as with joined waters, the opening must be as wide as a wineskin tube.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it is saying: if he does not need to immerse the outer vessel, then it is like joined waters, which are not joined until they are joined through an opening as wide as a wineskin tube.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the unclear phrase. 'Did not immerse' means the outer vessel did not need its own טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the משנה matches Step 8 exactly. An impure outer vessel makes the inner vessels pure no matter how narrow its opening is. A pure outer vessel works only if its opening is as wide as a wineskin tube, the same rule as for joining two bodies of water.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying (introduces a reading of the text)
He does not need to immerse it

steps.whatToRemember: An impure outer vessel 'carries' its טבילה to the vessels inside it, whatever the width of its opening. A pure outer vessel needs an opening as wide as a wineskin tube, just like two bodies of water that are being joined.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
and if he does not need to immerse it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the outer vessel, which was already pure.

phrases.english: then, like waters that are joined,
they are not joined until they are joined like the tube of a wineskin.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: וְאִם אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַטְבִּילוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10 and completes the proof for Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Did not immerse' means the outer vessel did not need טבילה because it was pure. In that case a wineskin-tube-wide opening is needed, as with joined waters.

steps.title: The argument of רבא and רבי אילא is an older argument between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the argument between רבא and רבי אילא was already argued by תנאים in a ברייתא about vessels immersed inside a basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argument of רבא and רבי אילא is an argument between תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: if someone filled a basket or a bin with vessels and immersed them, they are pure, both for קודש and for תרומה. אבא שאול says: they are pure for תרומה, but not for קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא links the argument of רבא and רבי אילא to a ברייתא. The first opinion there says such a טבילה works for everything, and אבא שאול says it works only for תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא lines up with רבא, who allows it even for קודש. אבא שאול lines up with רבי אילא, who is strict for קודש. So both אמוראים have support from an earlier תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is an argument between תנאים
A basket
A wicker bin, a large woven container
Sacrificial food, which needs the highest level of purity
The portion of produce given to a כהן; it needs purity, but less strictly than קודש

phrases.english: And this argument of Rava and Rabbi Ila
is an argument between tannaim.
As it is taught in a baraita: A basket or a wicker bin
that someone filled with vessels and then immersed them
whether for sacrificial food or for teruma, they are pure.
Abba Shaul says:
They are pure for teruma, but not for sacrificial food.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרָבָא וּדְרַבִּי אִילָא תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה in מקואות to show that the argument of רבא and רבי אילא already appears among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא holds that vessels immersed inside a basket are pure even for קודש, like רבא. אבא שאול holds they are pure only for תרומה, like רבי אילא.

steps.title: Then tell us why תרומה is not also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if there are real problems with immersing vessels inside vessels (the concerns of רבא and רבי אילא), why is the rule limited to קודש and not applied to תרומה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should be forbidden for תרומה too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the limit of the rule to קודש. If immersing vessels inside vessels is a real problem, for either רבא's reason or רבי אילא's, the problem should apply to תרומה as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concerns about this kind of טבילה are about whether the water really reaches every vessel. That is a physical question, so it should not matter whether the vessels are used for קודש or for תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is the reasoning
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, teruma too should be forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קודש/תרומה distinction comes up in the ברייתא of step 12, the גמרא challenges why the vessels-inside-vessels concerns are limited to קודש at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the ban on immersing vessels inside vessels applies only to קודש and not to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A physical problem with the טבילה should apply equally to both kinds of food.

steps.title: חברים already know how to immerse properly
steps.stepSummary: The rule is said to חברים, and they know well how to do it correctly, so there is no need to be strict about תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: To whom are we saying this rule? To חברים, and חברים know these things well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the people who follow these purity rules are חברים. They know how to immerse correctly, so no extra strictness is needed for תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חבר knows to make sure the basket's opening is wide enough and that nothing blocks the water. Because the people doing this are experts, there is no fear that the טבילה will go wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: People who carefully keep the laws of purity
They certainly know
To whom are we saying this?

phrases.english: To whom are we saying this? To ḥaverim,
and ḥaverim certainly know how to do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies who actually performs this kind of טבילה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The problem with the טבילה should apply to everyone and to all foods.
steps.terutzMaskana: The people doing it are expert חברים, so for תרומה we are not worried.

steps.title: Then קודש should be allowed too
steps.stepSummary: If חברים know how to immerse properly, why is immersing vessels inside vessels forbidden for קודש?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should be allowed for קודש too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around. If חברים can be trusted to immerse properly, then even for קודש there should be no problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 14 seems to prove too much. The same expert חברים also handle קודש, so the reason given should permit it there too.

phrases.english: If so, sacrificial food should be allowed too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that חברים know how to immerse properly
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the experts can be trusted, there is no reason to be strict about קודש either.

steps.title: An עם הארץ might copy the חבר
steps.stepSummary: For קודש we worry that an עם הארץ will see the חבר and immerse vessels the same way, but without the proper care.
steps.simpleTranslation: An עם הארץ will see him and go and immerse vessels this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the worry is not the חבר himself. The worry is an עם הארץ who watches him and copies him without knowing the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חבר does it correctly, but the onlooker sees only the outside of what he does. The onlooker will put vessels in a basket without checking the opening or what blocks the water, and his טבילה will not work.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person who is not careful about the laws of purity
He sees him
And he goes and immerses

phrases.english: An am ha'aretz will see him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the חבר who is immersing vessels inside a basket.

phrases.english: and he will go and immerse vessels this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזֵי לֵיהּ עַם הָאָרֶץ וְאָזֵיל מַטְבִּיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a concern about onlookers, not about the חבר himself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the חבר knows what he is doing, there should be no concern at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strictness exists so that an עם הארץ will not copy the חבר and immerse improperly.

steps.title: The same fear should apply to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: An עם הארץ could also watch a חבר immerse vessels for תרומה and copy him badly.
steps.simpleTranslation: For תרומה too, an עם הארץ will see him and go and immerse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. The fear about an עם הארץ copying the חבר should exist for תרומה as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 16 does not seem to depend on the kind of food. So the original question returns: why be strict only for קודש?

phrases.english: For teruma too,

phrases.aramaic: חָזֵי לֵיהּ עַם הָאָרֶץ וְאָזֵיל מַטְבִּיל!
phrases.english: an am ha'aretz will see him and go and immerse this way!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרוּמָה נָמֵי, חָזֵי לֵיהּ עַם הָאָרֶץ וְאָזֵיל מַטְבִּיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer about the עם הארץ copying
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The copying fear is just as real for תרומה, so it cannot explain why only קודש is treated strictly.

steps.title: We do not accept תרומה from an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: Bad copying does not matter for תרומה, because we never accept תרומה from an עם הארץ in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not accept it from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we do not accept תרומה from an עם הארץ at all, so it does not matter if he immerses his vessels incorrectly for תרומה. The next step challenges this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strictness exists only to protect the food that will actually be eaten in purity. An עם הארץ's תרומה is not trusted anyway, so his bad טבילה causes no harm there. That is why the strictness was made only for קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not accept from them

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on immersing vessels inside vessels is limited to קודש because of the fear that an עם הארץ might copy a חבר badly. This fear does not matter for תרומה, since we do not accept תרומה from an עם הארץ anyway.

phrases.english: We do not accept teruma from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17; the next step challenges this answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the concern does not cause any harm in the case of תרומה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The copying fear applies equally to קודש and תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For תרומה the copying does no harm, because an עם הארץ's תרומה is never accepted.

steps.title: Why not refuse קודש from an עם הארץ too?
steps.stepSummary: If we refuse תרומה from an עם הארץ and so don't worry about his bad copying, we should also refuse his קודש and stop worrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then for קודש too, let us simply not accept it from them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. If refusing תרומה from an עם הארץ solves the problem, refuse his קודש too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said bad copying doesn't matter for תרומה because we never take תרומה from an עם הארץ. The same fix could work for קודש. Then there would be no reason to be strict about immersing vessels inside vessels for קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacred food or items connected to the קרבנות of the מקדש
We should accept from them

phrases.english: Sacred food too, let us not accept from them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 18 and applies it to קודש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in steps 16 and 18 that the stringency exists for קודש because an עם הארץ might copy badly, while for תרומה his copying is harmless since his תרומה is refused.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If refusing an עם הארץ's תרומה removes the worry, refusing his קודש should remove it too.

steps.title: Refusing his קודש would cause resentment
steps.stepSummary: We cannot refuse קודש from an עם הארץ, because it would make him feel hostile.
steps.simpleTranslation: It would cause him resentment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that turning away an עם הארץ's קודש would make him resentful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a social reason not to refuse his קודש: it would create איבה between him and the חברים. So we must accept it, and the worry about bad copying stays.

keyTerms.meaning: Resentment or hostility between people
It will be for him, it will cause him

phrases.english: He would have resentment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a social reason that blocks the suggested fix
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could just refuse קודש from an עם הארץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: Refusing his קודש would cause איבה, so we accept it and must still worry about bad copying.

steps.title: Refusing his תרומה should also cause resentment
steps.stepSummary: If refusing קודש causes איבה, refusing תרומה should cause it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: With תרומה also, he would feel resentment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Refusing an עם הארץ's תרומה should upset him just as much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given for קודש seems to apply to תרומה as well. If so, we should not refuse his תרומה either. Then the difference between תרומה and קודש falls apart again.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: With תרומה too, he would have resentment!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from step 20 against the answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 18's claim that we never accept תרומה from an עם הארץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If איבה stops us from refusing קודש, it should stop us from refusing תרומה too.

steps.title: He can give his תרומה to a כהן friend
steps.stepSummary: An עם הארץ doesn't mind if a חבר refuses his תרומה, because he can give it to a כהן who is also an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not care, because he goes and gives it to a כהן who is an עם הארץ like him, his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that refusing תרומה causes no resentment. The עם הארץ has another place to give it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תרומה, there are many כהנים, so the עם הארץ just gives it to a friend and feels no rejection. With קודש there is only one מקדש, so turning him away really hurts. This explains why איבה matters for קודש and not for תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not care, it does not bother him
A כהן who is not careful about purity
His friend, his fellow

steps.whatToRemember: קודש: we must accept it from an עם הארץ to avoid איבה, so we worry about his bad copying. תרומה: we can refuse it with no איבה, so the worry falls away.

phrases.english: It does not bother him,
because he goes and gives it
to a כהן who is an עם הארץ, his friend.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אִיכְפַּת לֵיהּ, דְּאָזֵיל יָהֵיב לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן עַם הָאָרֶץ חַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 and closes this run of questions and answers.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the cases really are different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Refusing תרומה should cause the same איבה as refusing קודש.
steps.terutzMaskana: No איבה arises with תרומה, since the עם הארץ can give it to a כהן friend.

steps.title: Which תנא worries about resentment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that we take איבה into account.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who worries about resentment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks which תנא cares about איבה, so it can show where this idea comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answers above depended on the idea of avoiding איבה. Now the גמרא looks for a תנא who uses this idea elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Which תנא is this?
Who worries about, takes into account

phrases.english: And who is the תנא who worries about resentment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of the איבה idea used in steps 20 and 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that avoiding איבה shapes the halacha.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: everyone is trusted about wine and oil
steps.stepSummary: It is רבי יוסי. He says everyone is trusted about the purity of wine and oil all year, so people won't break away and make their own altar and פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יוסי. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי said, why is everyone trusted about the purity of wine and oil all year? So that each person will not go and build his own altar and burn his own פרה אדומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי is the תנא who worries about איבה. It quotes a ברייתא where he trusts even an עם הארץ about wine and oil, so that people are not pushed away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים refused wine and oil from an עם הארץ, he could feel shut out of the מקדש. He might then break away and set up his own altar and his own פרה אדומה. So רבי יוסי lets everyone be trusted, because keeping כלל ישראל together comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: Trusted, believed
The purity of wine and oil
A private altar outside the מקדש
The red heifer, burned to make ashes for purification

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a lasting principle: the חכמים sometimes relax rules to keep an עם הארץ from feeling pushed out and breaking away.

phrases.english: It is רבי יוסי.
As it is taught: רבי יוסי said:
For what reason is everyone trusted
about the purity of wine and oil
all the days of the year?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
phrases.english: So that each and every person will not
go and build an altar for himself,
and burn a red heifer for himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 and brings a ברייתא as support.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי, who trusts everyone about wine and oil so that people won't break away and build their own altars.

steps.title: Accepting testimony from an עם הארץ follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that our practice of accepting testimony from an עם הארץ follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Whose view do we follow when we accept testimony today from an עם הארץ? We follow רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a practical point. Accepting an עם הארץ as a witness today follows רבי יוסי's concern about איבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some might not trust an עם הארץ as a witness, because he is careless about halacha. But refusing him would cause איבה. Since we follow רבי יוסי, we accept his testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony
Nowadays, today
According to whom?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's concern about איבה is the basis for trusting an עם הארץ about wine and oil, and for accepting his testimony today.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
According to whom do we accept nowadays
testimony from an עם הארץ?
According to whom? According to רבי יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כְּמַאן מְקַבְּלִינַן הָאִידָּנָא סָהֲדוּתָא מֵעַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוסי's view from step 24 to today's practice with witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Accepting testimony from an עם הארץ today follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: What About Borrowed Vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: we should still worry that a חבר will borrow a vessel from an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us be worried about borrowing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the leniency about vessels used for תרומה. Even if a חבר never takes תרומה from an עם הארץ, he might borrow the עם הארץ's vessels and use them himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency rested on the idea that an עם הארץ's תרומה vessels do not matter to us, since we never accept his תרומה. But if a חבר borrows those vessels, a vessel that was not purified properly could end up touching the חבר's pure food. So the earlier reason does not fully cover every case.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us be worried about
Borrowing (here it does not mean 'a question')

steps.confusionAlert: Here שְׁאֵלָה means 'borrowing,' from the word שׁוֹאֵל, 'to borrow.' It is not the usual meaning of 'a question.'

phrases.english: But let us be concerned about borrowing!
phrases.notes: He means a חבר who borrows a vessel from an עם הארץ and then uses it for his own pure food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the reason given for leniency with תרומה vessels and challenges it from a new direction: borrowing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The leniency for תרומה vessels, which was based on the fact that a חבר does not accept תרומה from an עם הארץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even without taking his תרומה, a חבר may borrow an עם הארץ's vessel, so the vessel's purity still matters.

steps.title: The משנה About an Earthenware Vessel That Protects
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. בית הלל say an עם הארץ's כלי חרס protects everything inside it. בית שמאי say it protects only food, drink and other earthenware vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: An earthenware vessel protects everything inside it. That is what בית הלל say. בית שמאי say: It protects only food, drinks and earthenware vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that deals with the vessels of an עם הארץ. Its link to borrowing will become clear as the משנה continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sealed כלי חרס normally blocks טומאת מת from reaching what is inside it. בית הלל say this works for anything inside it. בית שמאי limit it to food, drink and other earthenware vessels, and the next lines explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: An earthenware (clay) vessel
Protects (from טומאה)
As we learned in a משנה
The students of שמאי and of הלל

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: כְּלִי חֶרֶס מַצִּיל עַל הַכֹּל,
phrases.english: As we learned: An earthenware vessel protects everything,
phrases.notes: The case is a tightly sealed clay vessel, belonging to an עם הארץ, sitting in a room with a dead body.

phrases.english: these are the words of בית הלל.
בית שמאי say: It does not protect
anything except food and drinks
and earthenware vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה about an עם הארץ's vessels in connection with the borrowing concern.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the borrowing of an עם הארץ's vessels is a real situation that matters
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עדיות about an earthenware vessel that protects from טומאת מת

steps.title: בית הלל Ask for the Reason
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל ask בית שמאי why they limit what the vessel protects.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: For what reason?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל ask בית שמאי to explain why they draw this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a sealed earthenware vessel protects whatever is inside it. So בית הלל want to know why בית שמאי treat food, drink and clay vessels differently from other items.

keyTerms.meaning: For what reason?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: בית הלל said to בית שמאי:
For what reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי מִפְּנֵי מָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind בית שמאי's view in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why בית שמאי limit the protection of the vessel to food, drink and earthenware vessels

steps.title: The Vessel Is טמא Because of the עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that the vessel is טמא because the עם הארץ handled it, and a טמא vessel cannot block טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said: Because it is טמא from the עם הארץ, and a טמא vessel does not block טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי give their reason: an עם הארץ's vessel counts as טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים treated anything an עם הארץ touches as טמא. Only a pure vessel can act as a barrier against טומאת מת. So, according to בית שמאי, this vessel should not protect anything at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is not careful about the laws of purity
Acts as a barrier, blocks
An impure vessel

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא
phrases.english: בית שמאי said: Because it is impure
on account of the עם הארץ,
phrases.notes: Literally 'on top of' the עם הארץ, meaning it became טמא through his handling.

phrases.english: and an impure vessel does not act as a barrier.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא עַל גַּבֵּי עַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית הלל's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עם הארץ's vessel is טמא, and a טמא vessel cannot block טומאה.

steps.title: But You Said the Food Inside Is Pure!
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל point out a problem: if the vessel cannot block טומאה, how can בית שמאי say the food and drink inside it stay pure?
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: But didn't you declare the food and drink inside it pure?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל challenge בית שמאי, saying their reason seems to contradict their own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a טמא vessel cannot act as a barrier, it should not protect anything, not even food and drink. Yet בית שמאי agree that food and drink inside it stay pure. That looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you...? (a word that opens a challenge)
You declared pure

phrases.english: בית הלל said to them:
But didn't you declare the food and drink inside it pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason בית שמאי just gave.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's reason that the vessel is טמא and cannot block טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the vessel cannot block טומאה, nothing inside it should stay pure, yet בית שמאי say food and drink do stay pure.

steps.title: בית שמאי Begin Their Answer
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי start to explain why they declared the food and drink pure. Their answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: When we declared the food and drink inside it pure,
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up בית שמאי's answer, which is finished in the next lines of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי are about to explain that their ruling about the food and drink rests on a special reason. That reason does not apply to the other items inside the vessel. Watch for how they finish the sentence.

keyTerms.meaning: When we declared pure

phrases.english: בית שמאי said to them:
When we declared the food and drink inside it pure —

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי כְּשֶׁטִּיהַרְנוּ אוֹכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to בית הלל's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining that the ruling has a limited scope (the answer is finished on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Declaring the food pure would mean the vessel itself counts as a barrier.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still to come: בית שמאי will explain the special reason behind their ruling about the food and drink.
